scope: Local implementation of FE-2a, the pure part of FE-2 (QR-3 slice S3 and QR-4 RO-7): the fixed-input evaluation contract builder and validator (mode FIXED_INPUT_EVAL, zero search, lineage, v1 policy equality, dataset binding), the versioned evaluation closure fixed-eval-closure-v1 with its hash, and a terminal-envelope job wrapper around the FE-1 evaluator. Nothing is imported by a runtime root, no worker or route runs it, and the existing engine-hash closures are unchanged.
method: Root accepted the FE-2 design decisions D1 to D6 (an independent architecture auditor, Opus 5.5, proposed them). A coder wrote FE-2a; the auditor reviewed it; an independent tester (Sonnet 5.5) ran single-edit mutations; one narrow fix round followed with a second tester check. The five existing engine hashes (LEGACY, FOUNDATION, INGESTION, PF-2 engine, PF-2 evaluator) were recomputed before and after each round and did not change. Nobody verified their own work.
hashNote: SHA-256 of the line-feed content as Git stores it.
result: node --test on the FE-2a JS tests and the parity test: 36 pass; pytest on test_fixed_eval.py and test_fixed_eval_job.py: 233 pass.

mutations.round1: 11 of 13 killed; 1 equivalent and 1 low gap (a getter on parent_policy in the getter-trap test).

limits: FE-2b (worker branch, admission, cancel, recovery and the runtime import) is not built; it rotates the FOUNDATION, INGESTION and PF-2 engine hashes when deployed, so it needs a release plan and an owner GO.
The eval job must stay unreachable until the shared exposure register exists (QR-3 S2).
Capacity at 10K bars on the VPS is unmeasured.
No staging readback and no PostgreSQL run.

rootAcceptance.statement: Root reviewed the agent reports and the final diff and accepted FE-2a as local engineering evidence. It changes no PM-1 credit by itself and starts no evaluation.
